name: timetackle
description: AI time tracking from your calendar: see timesheets and hours by client or project, and log time entries in your TimeTackle workspace.

interface.longDescription:
TimeTackle is AI time tracking built on your calendar. It tracks time automatically from your Google Calendar and Outlook events, with AI tag suggestions that sort it by client and project. Connect your TimeTackle workspace to ChatGPT to check your timesheets and log time without leaving the chat.

What you can do:
- Get your timesheet: hours per day and per project, client or tag, for you or your team.
- Break tracked time down by client, project, department or any of your tags, per person or per calendar.
- Log time in plain language: create, update and delete your manual time entries, with tags.
- Meeting time tracking: meeting hours, counts and trends by day, week or month.
- List your calendars and look up events with the same filters as the TimeTackle web app.

Who it is for: teams and individuals who use TimeTackle for calendar time tracking.

Limitations:
- You need a TimeTackle account; you sign in with it when you connect.
- Results cover only the calendars you can access in TimeTackle (owners and admins see the whole workspace; other members see the calendars, teams and people they were granted).
- Data exists only for your workspace's sync range; dates outside it return nothing.
- Manual entries are always created for the connected user.
- It does not create or change calendar events in Google or Outlook.

defaultPrompt: Show my timesheet for last week.
Break down my team's tracked time by client this month.
Log 1 hour today at 10am for project planning.

positive.description: Total meeting hours for a period
positive.prompt: How many hours of meetings did I have last week?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns total meeting hours for last week across the calendars the user can access, stating the date range used.

positive.prompt: Which calendars does TimeTackle track for me?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the imported calendars the connected user can access, by calendar email and title.

positive.prompt: How much time did each person spend on each client in the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Client property, then returns hours per person per client value (including untagged time where relevant), with names for each person.

positive.prompt: What is on my calendar tomorrow?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists tomorrow's events from the user's own calendars with times and titles, without inventing events.

positive.description: Log a manual time entry with a tag
positive.prompt: Log 1 hour today at 10am for 'Sprint planning', tagged Development.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a one-hour manual entry for the connected user tagged with the Development property and confirms it with the created entry's details.

negative.prompt: Pay my contractor $500 for last week's hours.

negative.description: Creating calendar meetings is not supported
negative.prompt: Book a meeting with Sam tomorrow at 3pm on my Google Calendar.
Show me the calendars and meetings of a TimeTackle workspace I am not a member of.

review.commerce_description: TimeTackle does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT. Users sign in to their existing TimeTackle account.

publication.release_notes: Listing copy now describes TimeTackle as AI time tracking from your calendar, with timesheets first. No tool changes.
